strongest_angle: Major entertainment unions are formally intervening in federal court to challenge OpenAI's fair use defense, arguing that unauthorized AI training on creative works constitutes a direct threat to the livelihoods of human creators.

key_facts.fact: On October 29, 2026, a memorandum of law was filed in the Southern District of New York by SAG-AFTRA, the American Federation of Musicians, and the Writers Guild of America regarding the OpenAI copyright litigation.
The unions jointly filed an amicus brief in the ongoing case In Re: OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation to urge the court to reject a categorical fair use exemption for AI model training.
The legal battle involves a coalition of news outlets and writers who allege that OpenAI scraped copyrighted material from the internet without authorization to train its large language models.
